name: Sacred Seasons: Holy Days and Pilgrimages of the Faiths
description: The fasts, feasts and journeys at the heart of the great religions, from Passover and Easter to Ramadan, Diwali and Vesak, and where and why each began.

checkpoints.name: Feasts of memory
checkpoints.note: Jews, Christians and Muslims all honour Abraham as a forefather. In Judaism, Passover recalls how Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt, Yom Kippur is a day of fasting and atonement, and pilgrims climb to Jerusalem. In Hinduism the Ganges is holy, Varanasi rises on its banks, and nearby the Buddha first teaches.

checkpoints.name: The Christian year
checkpoints.note: Jesus is crucified in Jerusalem at the time of Passover, and his followers, led by Saint Peter, proclaim that he rose again. Christianity marks this at Easter, celebrated from the second century, and a church council fixes how to set its date in 325. Both the Catholic Church and the Eastern Orthodox Church trace themselves to these years.

checkpoints.name: Lamps, colours and moons
checkpoints.note: In India the spring festival of Holi, with its colours, and the autumn festival of lamps, Diwali, are described in writing. Buddhism marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death at Vesak, recorded in Sri Lanka. In Arabia, Mecca is a trading town around the shrine of the Kaaba.

checkpoints.name: The Muslim year
checkpoints.note: Muhammad receives the first revelations of Islam in 610. The fast of Ramadan and the feast of Eid al-Adha are set in 624, and his pilgrimage of 632 shapes the rites of the Hajj. The Islamic calendar is lunar, so Ramadan moves through the seasons. In China the Mid-Autumn Festival takes form, and in India a Chinese traveller describes an early Kumbh Mela.

checkpoints.name: Two calendars and great crowds
checkpoints.note: The Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches split in 1054 and later follow different calendars, so their Easters often fall on different days. Rio Carnival turns the days before Lent into a samba parade. Today the Hajj gathers about two million pilgrims, and the Kumbh Mela draws crowds of many millions to bathe in sacred rivers.
